title: The Hours of Evening Close
description: The Hours of Evening Close in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Josiah Conder wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 957 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Saturday Evening”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The hours of eve-ning close; Its length-ened sha-dows, drawn O'er scenes of earth, in-vite re-pose, And wait the Sab-bath dawn.

lines: O'er scenes of earth, invite repose,
And, safe from violence and fear,
Will fold his flock to sleep.
And call us, strengthened by his might,
To pay the Lord our vows.

licence: Public domain: Josiah Conder died in 1855.
credits: Words by Josiah Conder (1789–1855), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
